structured_output.justification: The pricing trace correctly applies §1: a weight component of ₹6.00/kg on the shipment record's billed weight of 60kg (₹360) plus a distance component of ₹2.00/km on the booked lane distance of 85km (₹170), summing to the expected amount. The shipment carries no special_handling entries, so the cold chain premium under §3 correctly does not fire. There is no service-level premium issue since only standard service is offered (§2) and this shipment is standard. The billed amount exceeds this correctly-derived figure with no contractual basis identified for the difference, and nothing in the evidence points to an accessorial or surcharge that would explain it.

memo_narrative.what_happened: Sagar billed consignment SG-7003 above the amount produced by applying the contract's weight (₹6/kg) and distance (₹2/km) components to the shipment's actual 60kg/85km, with no cold chain or other surcharge applicable.
memo_narrative.why: Under §1 the freight charge is fixed as the sum of these two components, and §3's cold chain premium does not apply since the shipment has no special handling flagged — there is no clause that supports the higher billed figure.
memo_narrative.recommended_action: Request a corrected invoice from Sagar Roadlines for consignment SG-7003 citing §1, noting the cold chain premium in §3 does not apply to this shipment.
